summary: Most of the previous findings are fixed in the geometry. The top hatch gives real access to the shelf and the root bolts. The pod prints with 4 walls plus sleeve modifiers, so the FEA matches what prints. TWR is now computed for the prop actually fitted (HQ 7x4x3), the elevons are split with separate PETG horns, the outer segments bolt on with splice plates, and the pod has strap tabs and cooling vents. The fixes brought in new problems, though, and none of them is caught by a check. The new hatch is a flat 1.7 mm panel spanning 200 mm with nothing holding it down along its length, so it will balloon in flight. Its rear tongue covers the VTX antenna's exit hole. At one end of the elevon throw the pushrod runs into the servo pocket's aft edge. The outer elevon halves have about +-1.3 deg of free play on the slip-fit joiner. And the single PLA plate stacks the 7-hour pod with nine tall, thin standing parts.

findings.issue: The hatch (x -5 to 205, 72 mm wide, 1.7 mm PLA) is held only at its ends: 2 x M3 at x 4 and a tongue under the skin at x 205-213. Along its sides it just rests on the ledges (parts/pod.py ledge, parts/hatch.py), and nothing stops it lifting. The pod top sits above the wing's upper surface, in the suction field, and the bay is pressurised by the nose ram-air vents. So the net outward load is about 0.5-1.5 kPa at 100-150 km/h. As a 200 mm simply supported plate strip (I = 72 x 1.7^3 / 12 = 29.5 mm^4, E about 3 GPa), 500 Pa already gives about 7 mm of mid-span lift, and more at speed. The hatch will balloon, open a gap along both sides and buzz (oil-can) in flight. A 210 mm part that only has to stay down has no feature that keeps it down.
findings.fix: Add a second pair of M3 + inserts at mid-length. x 100-140 is clear of both sleeves at |y| 30-36: the main sleeve ends at about x 95 there and the rear sleeve starts at about x 155. Put ledge blocks there like the front ones. Also stiffen the panel: give it a slight crown (2-3 mm camber across the 72 mm) or two longitudinal 3 x 3 mm ribs at |y| about 25. They sit between the sleeves and the cut plane (2.8 mm), or are notched over the sleeves. Make the side edges overlap the ledges with a 0.5 mm lip so the gap is a labyrinth, not a slot.

findings.issue: The hatch's rear tongue covers the VTX antenna's exit hole. The tongue spans x 204-213 and |y| <= 30, 0.2 mm under the pod's top skin (hatch.py TONGUE_L = 8 from HATCH_X[1] = 205). The antenna hole is a 7 mm hole at x = ant_x = 212, y 0 (pod.py line 165), so x 208.5-215.5. The tongue is a separate part, so the hole is never cut through it, and 4.5 of the hole's 7 mm lie over the tongue. The antenna's 95 mm coax tube runs from the VTX's MMCX up through that hole, right where the tongue has to slide in. The hatch cannot be fitted with the antenna installed. The interference check misses it because the vtx_ant proxy starts at z = pod_top, above the skin.
findings.fix: Move ant_x to 220 (the param allows up to 225; check that the hole stays clear of the tail-top slope and the motor-mount bosses), or cut a 7.5 mm notch in the tongue at y 0. Let the vtx_ant proxy start at the VTX connector (z of the shelf + VTX height), so a future clash is caught.

findings.issue: At one end of the elevon throw the pushrod hits the servo pocket's aft edge. The servo pocket spans x 184.75-215.25 (tab span + 1, centred on servo_x 200). The output axis is at x 205.6, z 3.8, 8.2 mm above the lower skin (skin_z -4.4). DESIGN.md specifies an 8 mm arm hole and the horn hole 12 mm under the hinge (x about 268, z about -12.6). At +25 deg throw the horn hole moves about 5 mm aft, so the arm swings about 40 deg aft and its hole rises to z about -2.4. The pushrod line then crosses x 215.25 at z about -3.1, which is 0.65 mm inside the lower skin (-3.73 there), plus the wire's 0.6 mm radius. So the 1.2 mm wire runs into the pocket's aft wall, which is the 100 % modifier block, and the servo stalls at full throw in that direction. The build does not model the pushrod (report assembly.horns is empty), so nothing catches it. Also, the 8 mm KST arm hole is not in the catalog entry (servos.KST_X08_Plus has no arm geometry), and the static_torque requirement the last review asked for was not added. The 36 % servo load is a DESIGN.md hand calculation only. Applies to wing_r1.
findings.fix: Cut a pushrod exit slot through the lower skin from the pocket's aft wall to about x 235 (3 mm wide at y = horn_y, deep enough for the arm hole's full arc), or use a 10-11 mm arm hole with the 15 mm horn hole (same 1.4-1.5:1 ratio, hole lower). Catalog the KST arm's hole radii with a source. Add a static_torque requirement for servo_l / servo_r at the 0.20 N m hinge moment times the arm/horn ratio, and model the pushrod as a keep-out line swept with the elevon joint so the clash is checked.

findings.issue: The outer elevon halves (60 % of the surface, the outboard and most flutter-prone part) are driven only through the 3 mm carbon joiner. It is glued in the inner half and a slip fit in the outer half: the bore is JOINER_D + 0.25 (elevon.py line 63). The rod lies about 5.3 mm from the hinge axis (4 mm aft, 3.5 mm up), so 0.125 mm of radial clearance gives about +-1.35 deg of free rotation for the outer half about its hinge tape. Free play on a control surface is the classic cause of limit-cycle flutter and buzz, and this airframe is meant to fly at 150-180 km/h (DESIGN.md). The last review's free-play concern at the horn was fixed (1.3 mm holes) but moved here. Applies to elevon_ro.
findings.fix: Make the outer bore a zero-play fit and keep it removable: print it at 3.0 mm and ream it to a push fit, and lock it with a tape band across the split on both skins, or a 2 mm pin/grub screw across the joint. Better still, add a second, smaller rod (2 mm) further aft (about 15 mm from the hinge) so the two halves are keyed together at a long lever arm. Note the outer half's removal in the ASSEMBLY.md crash-repair step.

findings.issue: Plates are now one material each (fixed), but plate_2.3mf puts every PLA part in one job: the 310 mm pod, 4 wing segments standing 220-230 mm on 1-wall, 3 % infill, 4 elevon halves standing 126-189 mm on footprints about 40 x 5 mm, and the hatch standing 72 mm on a 1.7 mm edge. That is about 626 g and at least 400 min. On the A2L's moving bed, if any one slender part comes loose, the nozzle drags it through the others and the 312 g, 200-minute pod is lost with it. The last review asked for the pod alone and the tall parts kept apart. Only the material split was done.
findings.fix: Change export.plates (generally, not just for this project) to split a material group: put a part over about 200 mm tall or over about 3 h on its own plate, and keep tall slender parts (height/footprint > 15) apart from heavy ones. For this project: pod alone; wing segments 2 per plate; elevon halves + hatch together; PETG and TPU as now.

findings.issue: The ESC (73 mm long) cannot drop in from above. Between the sleeves the gap is only about 61 mm at y 0 and 60 mm at |y| 15 (main sleeve back edge about x 82-89, rear sleeve front about x 143-149), and in its final place the ESC sits partly under both sleeves (4 mm under their undersides). It goes in only by tilting it about 14 deg and sliding it under the rear sleeve, with 12 and 14 AWG leads already soldered. That works but is fiddly, and ASSEMBLY.md step 17 just says 'fit esc'. Also, 'one cable tie round the shelf' is impossible: the shelf runs wall to wall.
findings.fix: Add the tilt-and-slide instruction to step 17 (or shorten esc_x travel so the ESC sits between the sleeves, e.g. mounted on its side). Add two 3 x 1.5 mm cable-tie slots through the shelf beside the ESC.

findings.issue: Battery swap: the pack is reached only with the nose off (4 x M3 x 16 into inserts, every flight), and the strap's velcro sits 60-170 mm inside the bay with 6 mm over the pack, where you cannot close it by hand. That works only if the strap is a pre-closed loop the pack slides into, and nothing says so. A field battery swap that needs a hex key and 4 screws in a TPU nose will wear the inserts out.
findings.fix: In ASSEMBLY.md, say the strap is closed once into a snug loop through the tabs and the pack slides into it. Consider a quick-release nose: 2 screws plus a hook/tongue at the top, or captive thumb screws.

findings.issue: Mass margin is thin: TWR 1.54 against 1.5 allows only about 33 g of growth (1389 g). The 1356 g estimate (printed 726 + on-board 562 + wiring) does not include epoxy, foam tape, hinge tape, CA, heat-shrink, 18 brass inserts or about 22 screws, which is typically 20-35 g on a build like this. The real airframe will likely sit at TWR about 1.50-1.52 or below.
findings.fix: Add the consumables and fasteners to the mass model (bom_extra items with weight_g), or take mass out of the pod: it is 312 g and 'overbuilt' at 12 % utilisation; e.g. 3 walls in the hatch-side skins away from the bosses, or lightening windows in the shelf.

findings.issue: 26 inside corners are still sharp: 16 are declared (fillet would face down), 10 are not (vent slot corners at x 238, the shelf front at x -5 / y +-47, and the ledge ends at x -3). 6 of them are in stressed zones. At 12 % peak utilisation this is not a strength issue, but the vent corners in the belly are where landing cracks start.
findings.fix: Give the belly vents 2 mm end radii (slot shape instead of a box) and fillet or declare the rest.

findings.issue: The hatch prints standing on its 1.7 mm edge (363 mm2 contact, flagged by the build), 218 mm long and 72 mm tall. Printed flat on its outer face it would have a smooth bed-side finish on the visible top and no wobble.
findings.fix: Print it on its outer face (print_rot so the top skin is on the bed). The tongue then prints above its 3 mm root as a short cantilever, or give the root a 45 deg chamfer.

findings.issue: The splice plate is a 30 x 50 mm block standing about 3.5-5 mm proud of the lower skin, with exposed socket heads. It sits in the belly-landing slide zone. Only its plan-view edges are filleted, so its forward face is a square step that catches grass and adds drag. Same on splice_r.
findings.fix: Chamfer or round the leading and trailing lower edges (e.g. a 3 mm x 30 deg ramp at the front) and counterbore the screw heads flush.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: there is no TPU belly skid (brief: 'TPU where it lands'; the belly is PLA and only the nose is TPU). The RX's T antenna is still taped inside the pod beside the carbon tubes. The VTX output is not capped in DESIGN.md (800 mW in the pod, with a small inlet: two 8 mm nose vents).
findings.fix: Add a replaceable 2-3 mm TPU skid under the bay (bolted into the floor or glued). Route the RX antenna out through the wing root or the tail. Cap the VTX at 400-600 mW in DESIGN.md until a bench heat-soak test.

findings.issue: Stale or inconsistent documents. The mount_strength 'why' in project.yaml still describes 'the pylon carries the raised motor ... 24 mm above the upper pod bolts', but there is no pylon now. DESIGN.md says 'stock M3 x 6' for the motor screws, while ASSEMBLY.md and the fastener table use M3 x 5 (2 mm in the motor, exactly the catalog minimum). The DESIGN.md CG note still uses the 372 g pack ('372 / 1331 g'); the pack is now 302 g. The plate's outer edges have no edge break. report.maker_notes is still empty.
findings.fix: Rewrite the mount_strength why for the flush mount. Choose M3 x 6 (3 mm engagement, the max depth) in both places. Update the CG sensitivity (302 / 1356: about 2.2 mm of CG per 10 mm of pack). Add a 0.5 mm chamfer on the outer edges of the mount.

findings.issue: The 100 % modifiers are now in project.yaml and PRINT_SETTINGS.md (fixed in substance), but they are not written into the plate 3MF as modifier volumes. Each one has to be placed by hand in the slicer, 'sized and placed as below' from a text table, which is easy to miss on a 10-part plate.
findings.fix: Emit the modifier volumes into the per-part and plate 3MF (Bambu Studio supports modifier parts in the 3MF config).

findings.issue: Carried over: TE_MIN is still 1.0 mm (walls 0.97-1.04 mm flagged), which is fragile on a hinged surface that gets handled. The URDF joint and link names still collide (elevon_l / elevon_r).
findings.fix: TE_MIN 1.2 mm. Rename the URDF links (e.g. elevon_l_link).
